name: The Rolling Stones
description:
'''The Rolling Stones''' are an English [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in 1962. Active for over six decades, they are one of the most popular, influential, and enduring bands of the [[Album era|rock era]]. In the early 1960s, they pioneered the gritty, rhythmically driven sound that came to define [[hard rock]]. Their first stable line-up consisted of multi-instrumentalist [[Brian Jones]] vocalist [[Mick Jagger]], guitarist [[Keith Richards]],  bassist [[Bill Wyman]], and drummer [[Charlie Watts]], after keyboardist [[Ian Stewart (musician)|Ian Stewart]] was sidelined by manager [[Andrew Loog Oldham]] (though Stewart was retained as the band's road manager and session/touring keyboardist until his death in 1985). Jones was the leader in their early years. Oldham encouraged them to write their own songs, and the [[Jagger–Richards|Jagger–Richards partnership]] soon became the band's primary creative force.

Rooted in [[blues]] and [[rock and roll]], the Stones began by playing [[cover version| cover]]s and were at the forefront of the [[British Invasion]]. They found greater success with their own compositions: "[[(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction]]", "[[Get Off of My Cloud]]" (both 1965) and "[[Paint It Black]]" (1966) became international number-one hits. ''[[Aftermath (Rolling Stones album)|Aftermath]]'' (1966) was their first album of entirely original material. In 1967, they had the [[A-side and B-side|double-sided]] hit "[[Ruby Tuesday (song)|Ruby Tuesday]]"/"[[Let's Spend the Night Together]]" and experimented with [[psychedelic rock]] on ''[[Their Satanic Majesties Request]]''. They returned to their roots (grafted with [[folk music| folk]] and [[country music| country]]) with "[[Jumpin' Jack Flash]]" (1968) and "[[Honky Tonk Women]]" (1969). ''[[Beggars Banquet]]'' (1968) featured "[[Sympathy for the Devil]]" and "[[Street Fighting Man]]" and ''[[Let It Bleed]]'' (1969) featured "[[Gimme Shelter]]" and "[[You Can't Always Get What You Want]]".

Jones left the band a few weeks before his death in 1969, and was replaced by guitarist [[Mick Taylor]]. That year, they were introduced on stage for the first time as "[[Honorific nicknames in popular music|the Greatest Rock and Roll Band in the World]]". In 1970, they formed [[Rolling Stones Records]], for which their famous [[tongue and lips logo]] was created. ''[[Sticky Fingers]]'' (1971), their first album on the label, yielded "[[Brown Sugar (Rolling Stones song)|Brown Sugar]]" and "[[Wild Horses (Rolling Stones song)|Wild Horses]]" and was their first of eight consecutive number-one studio albums in the US. It was followed by ''[[Exile on Main St.]]'' (1972), featuring "[[Tumbling Dice]]" and "[[Happy (Rolling Stones song)|Happy]]", and ''[[Goats Head Soup]]'' (1973), featuring "[[Angie (song)|Angie]]". Taylor left the band at the end of 1974 and was replaced by [[Faces (band)|Faces]] guitarist [[Ronnie Wood]]. 

''[[Some Girls]]'' (1978) showed the influence of [[punk rock|punk]] and [[disco]] with "[[Miss You (The Rolling Stones song)|Miss You]]", "[[Beast of Burden (song)|Beast of Burden]]", and "[[Shattered (song)|Shattered]]". ''[[Tattoo You]]'' (1981) produced "[[Start Me Up]]". ''[[Steel Wheels]]'' (1989) and ''[[Voodoo Lounge]]'' (1994) were promoted by large stadium and arena tours. Following Wyman's departure in 1993, the band continued as a four-piece core, with [[Darryl Jones]] becoming their bassist, releasing ''[[Bridges to Babylon]]'' (1997) and ''[[A Bigger Bang]]'' (2005). By 2007, they had broken the record for the all-time [[List of highest-grossing concert tours|highest-grossing concert tour]] three times, and they were the highest-earning live act of 2021, with [[Steve Jordan (drummer)|Steve Jordan]] becoming their regular drummer following Watts' death that year. ''[[Hackney Diamonds]]'' (2023) became their [[List of artists by number of UK Albums Chart number ones|fourteenth UK number-one album]]. ''[[Foreign Tongues]]'' (2026) was their fifteenth.

The Rolling Stones have estimated album sales of more than 250 million. They have won four [[Grammys]] and a [[Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award]]. They were inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1989 and the [[UK Music Hall of Fame]] in 2004. [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']] and ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' have ranked them as one of the greatest artists of all time.
